All frequently asked questions

Nothing on this page matches that. Ask us, and the answer goes up here.

The basics

AI that does tasks for you, rather than only answering questions. You message it the way you would text a friend and it handles the job: the inbox, a reminder, a lookup. It answers ordinary questions too, the way any AI chat does.
None. Setting up an agent is answering a few questions about what it is for, and add-ons are written in plain words rather than code. If you want to know how it works underneath, we will go as deep as you like.
You will understand it, because a guided session is built for that. We walk through what it can and cannot do, and why we make each choice, while you watch it happen on your own computer. You leave able to change it yourself. What a session involves →
It runs on your computer, on an AI account of your own. It asks your permission before an email goes out or your calendar changes: email waits for your Send or a time you set, and a calendar change waits for your approval. Neither is a setting. How the other nine handle both →
You would not. Keep the apps you like. The difference is that they wait for you to check them: your car registration renewal sits in an email you skimmed three weeks ago. Your agent catches the deadline, puts it on your list, and messages you before it lapses.
Keep it. Archie runs on a schedule on your own computer and reaches you first. If your problem is one hard task, a work tool is the right call. If it is that small things keep slipping, Archie is built for that. Side by side →

Look in its settings for words like approval, permission or ask first, and read what each choice allows. Then look for a choice that stops the asking, such as “always allow” on an approval prompt.

Four questions are worth asking any agent, and we wrote where to look for each, with Archie’s answer beside it. Check the agent you already have →

On somebody’s computer. Some agents work on a computer their company runs, and keep working with every device you own switched off. An agent’s help pages will say so, with words like cloud, server or virtual machine.

Archie works on your own computer, while it is awake. Your conversations go to your AI company, and we keep no copy we can read. How other agents answer →

Its company’s privacy page is the place to look: what it keeps, where, for how long, and whether what you send is used to train its AI.

On Archie, your agent’s files and chat history live on your computer, and what you ask goes to the AI company you pick. We hold a little, and none of it is a conversation we can read. The whole list →

Add-ons

They do not talk to each other. Each add-on does its one job and hands the result back, and your agent decides what goes to the next one, or calls several at once and puts what they send together.
Because “everything” is hundreds of unrelated jobs under one word. Separate add-ons let your agent reach for the one that fits the job in front of it, and you can still add all the ones you want.
Each add-on says what it is for, and your agent picks the one that fits the task.

Cost & billing

The discovery call is free, 30 minutes, no obligation. A guided session is $250 an hour, and a bigger setup takes more sessions rather than a higher rate. The Archie app is free on an AI account of your own at 20 jobs a day. A plan takes that limit off for $30 a month or $299 a year, bought separately from sessions. Every cost, in full →

Yes, in two ways. Free credits, for up to 14 days or until they run out: no card, and Claude usage on our account. So those messages pass through our server, and email and text reading are off while we are paying.

Or, on Personal, free on an AI account of your own with no end date: every skill and routine at 20 jobs a day, starting again at midnight, without phone access. That AI company bills you for what your agent uses. How the free tier works →

No. The app is a separate plan: Personal is $30 a month or $299 a year, Business $99 a month or $999 a year; guided sessions cover our time building your agent with you. A session is worth having whether or not you keep the app running afterwards.
Yes, on the app: email us within 14 days of first starting a plan and we refund it in full. After that you stop a plan from the Account page, and it ends when the period you paid for does. Guided sessions are hours already spent with you, so they are not refundable. What stopping looks like, step by step →
Yes. You pay your AI company directly for what your agent does. That is $1 to $5 a month for a handful of tasks a day, $21 to $42 with a calendar and inbox connected, and $64 to $139 for one wired into a whole working day. Where those figures come from →
A subscription works inside that company’s own app and cannot be used by a program you own. An AI account of your own can: you pay for what you use, often less than a subscription, and your own subscription keeps working as normal. What each company does with what you send it is quoted on the Trust page.

Safety & privacy

Only the ones you connect. You connect each one yourself in Archie, or with us in a guided session, and can disconnect any of them at any time.

It drafts, and you decide what goes out. A text goes out only when you tap Send, and an email when you send it or set a time. A calendar change applies only after you approve it in a later message, never while you are away.

Buying is off until you switch it on. Then it can place an order, only at shops you pick, up to the limits you set, and only after you tap to approve that order from Archie, your phone, or your chat app.

It never types a card number. The limit is checked against the price it reads on the page, so for a hard ceiling give it a card from your bank that works at one shop. What that looks like at a checkout → The honest limits on that gate →

A fair thing to ask about software you are about to give your calendar to. Your agent is in one conversation, the one with you, and it is not awake in between: three things start it, and nothing runs between them.

It cannot run a program on your computer or make calls and texts, and it buys only if you switch that on, only at shops you pick, only up to a limit you set. None of that promises it will always be right, which is why anything it sends in your name, and any change to your calendar, waits for you. What enforces each one →

Review drafts and proposals before approving them, because a sent message or an approved change may not be reversible. If we set your agent up with you, tell us what went wrong and we will help put it right.

We hold a little, and none of it is a conversation we can read. Your agent’s files and chat history live on your computer, and your key goes only to your AI company.

On an AI account of your own, your agent’s thinking goes straight to that company. Free credits, and the plan with the AI included, run through a server of ours, which measures spend without recording what was said.

What we hold is your email address, your plan, a handful of operational records, and, if phone access is on, sealed messages we cannot read. The whole list →

It lives in a folder on your computer, behind your own login, and behind disk encryption if you turned it on, with your key in your computer’s password store rather than in a file. If the computer is lost, reset that key on the AI company’s site and disconnect the accounts.

We keep no backup of it: Archie can write one under Backups, and it is an ordinary file, so keep it where you would keep a tax return. What travels and what does not →

Timeline & what to expect

A guided walkthrough is one hour. Larger builds are split into phases, with an estimated number of sessions and total cost given after the free discovery call. You can begin with one useful workflow and add accounts or jobs later.
Yes. Start with one or two jobs that matter most, then add more once those are working.
Archie can work with connected email, calendars, files, chat apps and the add-ons in its public catalog. Jobs it can take on include morning briefings, meeting preparation, research, reminders and drafting replies for your approval. Browse the current catalog or see how it works.
Tell us. We scope it and quote a price before we build the add-on, and it can then join the shelf for everyone after you. Commission an add-on to get started.
Once it is running it mostly looks after itself. The part worth your attention is deciding what to trust your agent with, and that goes as far as you want. After setup, questions about anything we set up with you are answered free, with no time limit, and new work is scoped and priced first.

Practical details

No. You need a computer you are happy to leave on and connected; a Mac mini is the easy answer, never the requirement. The computer you have may well do: it spends most of its life idle, so it need not be fast or new. Answer a few questions and we will lay out your kit →

You stop a plan on Archie’s Account page, and it runs to the end of the period you paid for. On Personal, with your own AI key saved, Archie keeps opening after that, free at 20 jobs a day, and every agent you made keeps working. Without a saved key it asks for one, and Archie for Business asks for a plan.

Nothing on your computer is deleted in any of the three, but write your backup before you stop, since it is made from inside Archie. If we cease operations, our Terms promise “a final version of Archie that requires no license check, within 30 days of shutting down.” All of it, in one place →

Whichever you already use. Archie works with Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix and, on a Mac, iMessage, and Telegram is the easiest to start with. You can also talk to your agent inside Archie: it is the same conversation either way, so there is no wrong pick and no rush to make one.

Any of the seven can run your agent. To switch later, tell your agent “use ChatGPT instead” and it does, once you have a key for that company, after a restart of a few seconds.

Its skills, routines and memory stay as they are, because they sit on your computer. If you are unsure, Claude is a sensible default: the free credits run on it, and it is the one that can read scanned PDFs. What each company does with your words →

Start on Balanced, and change it any time. Economy is quick and cheapest for simple work; Best uses the most capable model at a higher cost per message. If you are moving the dial to save money, know that an add-on can pick its own level and ignore it: the checkbox underneath is what overrides them. What that is worth, measured →

Yes to both: your agent runs on your computer rather than on ours, so it answers while that computer is on, awake and connected. Archie can also wake it for a routine set for a time. A laptop is fine, plugged in with sleep set to Never, and a cable from the router beats Wi-Fi because every drop is time your agent spends stopped.

If it does stop, it picks up by itself when the computer comes back, with nothing for you to set up again.
